newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Return to IMF crucial for Yugo economic progress.
newsitem.headline: Return to IMF crucial for Yugo economic progress.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Prime Minister Radoje Kontic, central bank members and government officials say restoring ties with international financial institutions as soon as possible is imperative for economic development.

"Urgent normalisation of ties with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Trade Organisation (WTO) is the top priority of the country's economic policy," the Federal Information Ministry said in a statement late on Tuesday, carried by the official Tanjug news agency.

"Fast return to the international community and activating membership in the IMF and WTO is the most important condition for Yugoslavia's return to world finances and a guarantee of future economic development," the statement said.
Yugoslavia, which is accumulating virtually no domestic capital, can attract fresh capital only after regulating its ties with world financial organisations, the statement said.
Fresh foreign capital was seen key to greater investment activity, improvement of quality and increased competitiveness of the Yugoslav economy on the world markets.
"Fast and dynamic development of the Yugoslav economy...is also the only guarantee to resolve growing economic and social problems.

"Restructuring of the economy and the banking sector have an important role in the development policy, without which Yugoslavia could not transform into a modern and competitive market-oriented economy," the statement said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
